compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

In a git checkout, `rebar --version` reports the commit of the FIRST build of that checkout, not the checked-out commit. Observed 2026-11-23 PST in the `cli-main` worktree: HEAD `915a63bfa10` (Release 0.17.0), `make install` exit 0, yet `rebar --version` printed `rebar 0.17.0 (91322a91e9e)`, a commit from 2026-11-19. `src/rebar/_build_info.py` still held `COMMIT = '91322a91e9e'`.

Cause in the code: `hatch_build.py` `_resolve_build_commit` precedence step 2 PRESERVES an existing non-null `COMMIT` in `_build_info.py` before trying step 3 (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`). Step 2 exists for the rebuild-from-sdist path (no `.git`), but it also fires in a checkout that has `.git`, so once a value is baked every later editable reinstall keeps it. `_version_line()` in `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py` reads only `_build_info.COMMIT`.

Release wheels are not affected: `release.yml` sets `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` (step 1); a fresh `pipx install nava-rebar[mcp]==0.17.0` reported `915a63b` correctly. Not yet checked: whether `rebar.signing`'s gate-code SHA resolver reads the same stale file in a checkout (its docstring says the live checkout SHA wins when present).

## Approach

Investigate with a reproduction first (build twice in a temp git repo across a commit; assert the second build bakes the new HEAD). Then make the live git SHA win over the preserved value whenever the build root is a git work tree, keeping step 2 for the no-`.git` sdist rebuild. Check whether `rebar.signing` is affected and cover it if so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test reproduces the stale bake: two builds in one git work tree across a commit bake the second HEAD's short SHA; fails before the fix.
- [ ] The rebuild-from-sdist path (no `.git`, existing baked SHA, no env var) still preserves the baked SHA (existing coverage keeps passing).
- [ ] In a checkout, after a commit and `make install`, `rebar --version` reports `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
- [ ] Whether `rebar.signing`'s gate-code SHA can read a stale `_build_info.py` in a checkout is recorded with evidence, and fixed in this ticket if it can.
compiled_state.title: rebar --version in a git checkout reports the first build's commit: hatch_build preserves a stale baked COMMIT over git HEAD
